title: Meet Hangul
description: Read a syllable block and discover the jobs of its letters.

blocks.title: Letters form blocks
blocks.text: Hangul is an alphabet whose letters combine into syllable blocks. Each block has an initial consonant and a vowel; a final consonant is optional. Read blocks left to right in ordinary horizontal text.

blocks.title: Silent first, audible last
blocks.text: ㅇ is silent at the beginning of 아, but sounds like ng at the end of 강. Its position changes its role.

blocks.title: Writing and sound
blocks.text: Romanization is a temporary reading aid. Korean sounds do not map perfectly to English letters. Audio uses a Korean device voice when available; it is not a verified recording. Stroke demonstrations require verified assets; unverified paths are never supplied.

exercises.prompt: What does one Hangul block usually represent?
exercises.explanation: A block combines consonant and vowel letters.

exercises.prompt: What is initial ㅇ doing in 아?
exercises.explanation: Final ㅇ is ng, but initial ㅇ is silent.

title: Basic consonants
description: Recognize fourteen basic consonants in short words.

blocks.title: Your basic consonants
blocks.text: Read ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ ㅂ ㅅ ㅇ ㅈ ㅊ ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅎ. Their names and sounds are different: ㄱ is called 기역, but that name is not the sound you insert into a word.
blocks.korean: ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ ㅂ ㅅ ㅇ ㅈ ㅊ ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅎ

blocks.title: Learn sounds in words
blocks.text: ㄱ varies with position and is not always English g. ㄹ can be a short tap or an l-like sound. Aspirated ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ have a stronger puff than their plain counterparts. Use the character cards for examples and recall mastery.

exercises.prompt: Which consonant begins 마?
exercises.explanation: 마 is ㅁ plus ㅏ.

exercises.prompt: Which consonant begins 나무 (tree)?
exercises.explanation: 나 begins with ㄴ.

exercises.prompt: Which is the aspirated counterpart of ㄱ?
exercises.explanation: ㅋ is aspirated; ㄲ is tense, not the same contrast.

title: Basic vowels
description: Recognize ten basic vowels and their orientation.

blocks.title: Ten basic vowels
blocks.text: Learn ㅏ ㅑ ㅓ ㅕ ㅗ ㅛ ㅜ ㅠ ㅡ ㅣ. A vertical vowel usually sits beside the consonant; a horizontal vowel usually sits underneath it.
blocks.korean: 아 야 어 여 오 요 우 유 으 이
blocks.reading: a ya eo yeo o yo u yu eu i

blocks.title: Distinguish rather than guess
blocks.text: ㅓ (eo) is not the same as ㅗ (o). ㅡ (eu) is not English oo. Listen when a Korean voice is available and compare 우 and 으; romanization alone cannot teach the contrast.

exercises.prompt: Which block contains ㅗ?
exercises.explanation: 오 combines silent ㅇ and ㅗ.

exercises.prompt: Which block contains ㅡ?
exercises.explanation: 으 has the vowel eu.

exercises.prompt: Which vowel normally goes to the right of the initial consonant?
exercises.explanation: Compare 가 and 고.

title: Build syllable blocks
description: Combine consonants and vowels into readable words.

blocks.title: Beside or underneath
blocks.text: ㄴ + ㅏ becomes 나. ㄱ + ㅗ becomes 고. These letters share one block, rather than being written as a row of separate letters.

blocks.title: Read meaningful words
blocks.text: 나무 has two blocks, 나 and 무. 바다 means sea. 우유 means milk. A word can have several syllables; a syllable does not automatically have its own English meaning.

exercises.prompt: What is ㄴ + ㅏ in one block?
exercises.explanation: The vertical vowel is beside ㄴ.

exercises.prompt: Build 나무 (tree) from syllable tiles.
exercises.explanation: 나 + 무 forms 나무, tree.

exercises.prompt: How many syllable blocks are in 우유?
exercises.explanation: 우 and 유 are separate blocks.

title: Final consonants: batchim
description: Read a final consonant and notice connected pronunciation.

blocks.title: The bottom position
blocks.text: 받침 is the final consonant position below the vowel. In 강, ㅇ is the final ng. In 산, ㄴ is the final n.

blocks.title: Spelling and connected sound
blocks.text: Several written finals share the same unreleased final sound. When followed by a vowel-initial syllable, a final consonant may connect to it: 밥을 is pronounced 바블. Double finals and sound changes need word-specific study; do not pronounce every final with an extra vowel.

exercises.prompt: What is the batchim in 강?
exercises.explanation: The bottom ㅇ is ng.

exercises.prompt: Which word means mountain?
exercises.explanation: 산 ends with ㄴ.

exercises.prompt: How should a final consonant be practiced?
exercises.explanation: Learn the final and its connected pronunciation in a word.

title: Compound vowels
description: Read common compound vowels in everyday words.

blocks.title: Combine vowel shapes
blocks.text: Learn ㅐ ㅒ ㅔ ㅖ ㅘ ㅙ ㅚ ㅝ ㅞ ㅟ ㅢ. In modern speech ㅐ and ㅔ may sound alike for many speakers; keep the spelling distinction.

blocks.title: Read in context
blocks.text: 과자 includes ㅘ, 귀 includes ㅟ, and 의자 begins with ㅢ. The pronunciation of ㅢ varies with position and grammatical use; learn 의자 as a whole word before particle 의.

exercises.prompt: Which block contains ㅘ?
exercises.explanation: ㅗ plus ㅏ forms ㅘ.

exercises.prompt: Which word means chair?
exercises.explanation: 의자 begins with ㅢ.

exercises.prompt: If ㅐ and ㅔ sound similar, should their spellings be merged?
exercises.explanation: Pronunciation overlap does not erase spelling distinctions.

title: Tense consonants
description: Distinguish plain, aspirated, and tense consonants.

blocks.title: Five tense consonants
blocks.text: ㄲ ㄸ ㅃ ㅆ ㅉ are tense consonants. They are not simply longer English consonants, and not the same as aspirated ㅋ ㅌ ㅍ ㅊ. Listen to complete words before trying to explain the contrast using English letters.

blocks.title: The contrast can change meaning
blocks.text: 달 is moon; 딸 is daughter. 쌀 is uncooked rice, while 살 has several meanings, including flesh and the age counter. Learn the intended meaning in context.

exercises.prompt: Which word means daughter?
exercises.explanation: 딸 begins with tense ㄸ.

exercises.prompt: Which word means uncooked rice?
exercises.explanation: 쌀 begins with tense ㅆ.

exercises.prompt: Which consonant is tense?
exercises.explanation: ㅂ is plain, ㅍ aspirated, and ㅃ tense.

title: Read Korean words
description: Decode useful signs and practice comprehension.

blocks.title: A sign-reading mission
blocks.text: Read without romanization first. 입구 is entrance, 출구 is exit, and 약국 is pharmacy. 서울역 is Seoul Station; its connected pronunciation differs from spelling letter by letter.

blocks.title: Reading before speed
blocks.text: Break unfamiliar words into blocks, connect them, then check meaning. If your device has no Korean voice, read aloud yourself; silent reading is not proof of listening comprehension.

exercises.prompt: Which sign leads to the exit?
exercises.explanation: 출구 is exit; 입구 is entrance.

exercises.prompt: You need a pharmacy. Which sign do you seek?
exercises.explanation: 약국 is a pharmacy.

exercises.prompt: Which word includes station?
exercises.explanation: 역 means station.

title: Write useful vocabulary
description: Rebuild familiar words, type them, and compare your handwriting.

blocks.title: Read, build, type, recall
blocks.text: Begin with tiles, then type the same word using a Korean keyboard, then choose independent mode. Korean input normally composes jamo into NFC syllables. Finish IME composition before checking.

blocks.title: Honest handwriting feedback
blocks.text: Independent mode includes an optional drawing canvas. Compare with a printed model yourself. This records self-reviewed practice only; it is not stroke-order verification, automatic handwriting recognition, or a currency reward.

exercises.prompt: Build 한국어 (Korean language).
exercises.explanation: 한 + 국 + 어 forms 한국어.

exercises.prompt: Type 가방 (bag), then try independent mode.
exercises.explanation: 가방 has two blocks.

exercises.prompt: Write 커피 (coffee) independently.
exercises.explanation: Use the model to self-review the two blocks.

title: Build Korean sentences
description: Move from guided explanations to tiles, gap filling, independent typing, and optional handwriting.

blocks.title: Level 1 · Understand the roles
blocks.text: Korean normally places the predicate last. 저는 is a topic; 제가 is a subject form. 은/는 follows a final consonant/vowel respectively. 이/가 follows a final consonant/vowel respectively. 을/를 marks many objects. Topics are not simply the same thing as subjects.

blocks.title: Level 2 · Arrange words
blocks.text: Build a complete model with tiles. 학생이에요 follows a final consonant; 가수예요 follows a vowel. Polite questions can keep statement order and use rising intonation.

blocks.title: Level 3 · Fill a gap
blocks.text: For the gap 저는 커피를 ___, supply 마셔요. 먹다 → 먹어요, 가다 → 가요, 하다 → 해요. Place 안 before an ordinary verb to negate it: 안 마셔요. Do not replace a noun negation 학생이 아니에요 with 안 학생이에요.

blocks.title: Level 4 · Write independently
blocks.text: Time often comes early. 에 marks destination or many time points; 에서 marks where an action occurs. 어제 and 내일 take no time 에. Past 가다 → 갔어요; future 가다 → 갈 거예요, 먹다 → 먹을 거예요.
blocks.translation: Yesterday I studied at a café.

blocks.title: Level 5 · Optional handwriting
blocks.text: In independent mode, write on the canvas or on paper and compare to the model. Account completion records practice, not verified penmanship. Stroke order remains review-required until sourced assets are attached.

exercises.prompt: In 저는 책을 읽어요, what does 을 mark?
exercises.explanation: 책 ends in a consonant, so it takes 을.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: I am a student.
exercises.explanation: 학생 ends in a consonant: 학생이에요.

exercises.prompt: Fill the gap: 저는 커피를 ___. Type only the missing polite verb for drink.
exercises.explanation: 마시다 becomes 마셔요.

exercises.prompt: Arrange: There is a book here.
exercises.explanation: 책 takes subject 이; 에 marks its location.

exercises.prompt: Write: I do not drink coffee.
exercises.explanation: 안 negates 마셔요. The topic may be omitted when clear.

exercises.prompt: Arrange the question: Where is the restroom?
exercises.explanation: 이 marks the subject and 에 the location.

exercises.prompt: Write: Yesterday I studied at a café.
exercises.explanation: Use 에서 for the action location and 했어요 for past 하다.

exercises.prompt: Write: Tomorrow I will go to school.
exercises.explanation: 에 marks the destination; 갈 거예요 expresses the plan.
